utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination continues with Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would particularly like to greet His Honour Judge Lindholm, who is back with us, and I would indeed like us to continue in this way and for him to be present during our proceedings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed the financing in the SDA. However, after going through what we have been talking about yesterday, one question remained unanswered, and I would like to ask this question now in order to get your response. Yesterday you said that the list of the citizens who had organised themselves was made by you in late September, October, or perhaps even early November, and when I -- I mean 1991- and when I asked you about the absence of Serbs, you said that there were no Serbs there but that there were Serbs on later lists. Can you please tell me now: What was this list that was made later which contained members of the Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there were other lists that were made in the period when the Territorial Defence of Bosanski Samac was set up. Of course, these lists were not found in my briefcase, which was found when my apartment was looted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please remember and tell me some of the names of the ethnic Serbs that were on the list as of the 14th or 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that the list was compiled in the period between the 10th of April and the 16th of April, 1992. I did not have the lists with me. The lists were in the possession of another person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand. But if you had seen the list and if you claim that there were such persons there, could you please enumerate some of the ethnic Serbs that were on the list.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th or the 14th of April, 1992, when the Territorial Defence of the Bosanski Samac municipality was set up, I convened a meeting of the preliminary war staff of the Bosanski Samac municipality. In this pre-war staff of the Bosanski Samac Territorial Defence, there were 16 or 17 reserve officers who were ethnic Serbs, 2 or 3 Muslims, and 2 or 3 Croats. At that meeting, the new leadership of the Territorial Defence, Mr. Marko Bozanovic and myself, talked to the then members of the war staff of the Territorial Defence, which was not functioning. Among those people, some officers who were ethnic Serbs, who were on the war staff, also attended the meeting. Please allow me. My next sentence will contain the name that you want. The loyalty, if I may call it that, to the new Territorial Defence, was pledged by Captain Savic. He had a construction degree -- civil engineering degree. His sister was a doctor. I can't recall his name now. Could you please assist me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean Cvijetin Savic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Cvijetin Savic. So he agreed to work in the staff of the newly formed Territorial Defence. Vidak Prusina also signed. I have to say I don't know what ethnic group he belongs to. I'm now talking about the officers. On the 13th, 14th, 15th, and 16th, in Room 1, a person was charged by the newly formed Territorial Defence, a person of Serb ethnicity, who registered new members of the Territorial Defence. So it was that person's task. Among them was a large number of members of the new Territorial Defence who were of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, my question was the following: On some lists of the citizens who organised themselves, there were some Serbs. That's what you said. Now we're talking about the establishment of the Territorial Defence. Can you remember which ethnic Serbs did, on the 13th, 14th, 15th, and 16th, volunteer to report to the Territorial Defence staff and was entered on the list?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, on the 13th, 14th, 15th, and 16th, I was not interested in the ethnic background of the newly registered members of the Territorial Defence. What I was interested in was their number, not their ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that there were Serbs among them. That's why I'm asking you this question.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the information that I received from the employee or clerk who registered the people who reported to join the Territorial Defence, and that employee was of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us the name of that employee, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember. He was the member of the old Territorial Defence, and he also agreed to join the newly formed Territorial Defence. His last name is Dujmusic, his father's name is Janko, and now I'd like you to remind me of his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that it was Darko Dujmusic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Darko Dujmusic is the child of a mixed marriage? His father is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. But can we agree that Mr. Vidak Prusina is a Croat, an ethnic Croat who had come to Samac from Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I never cared for one's ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet you do know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I've already told you: If you don't know something, you just say "I don't know. I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you told me to answer you with yes or no, and now you got me to tell you stories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this information that a certain number of Serbs volunteered to join the new Territorial Defence, you got that information from Darko Dujmusic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if the weapons for the arming of your unit was procured from the Republic of Croatia, from the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not procured by the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If my information is correct, Mr. Atic Ratif was a member of your unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit D6/4 and D6/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I would like to ask you to put this document on the ELMO. You have already seen this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirm that this is the certificate of issuance number 1342, from the 2nd of March, 1992, that the name here is Ratif Atic, that it was issued in warehouse 1, and that the items listed here -- now I would like to ask you one thing: Do you see a stamp on this certificate?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but it is not really very legible. I don't see the number that you referred to, number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Now I see it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This stamp here at the bottom of the document, could you please read what is written on the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness have a closer look?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you want you can take it in your hand and take a closer look?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says military post code Slovanski Brod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number is also listed here, the number of the military post code?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really see it. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military post code Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a stamp that was used in the military?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's suppose that it was. I'm not sure, but it does say here "military post code." It was used in the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do agree with me that Slavonski Brod is a town in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read here what it says under the name "warehouse operator." Can you please read the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that person whose last name is Vrljic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he is your friend, can you please tell us what is his first name?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivo Vrljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us: Where does he come from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this document was issued by Mr. Vrljic in the warehouse in Slavonski Brod; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and he issued it to Ratif Atic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Atic -- Ratif Atic bring the ammunition that he took over to your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take the document away. We won't be needing it any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to mention one thing for the record. At page 5, line 7, the question was if any weapons for the arming of your unit were provided from the Republic of Croatia. Then counsel got into this. This concerns bullets. I just want to make sure that this is not being used as a prior inconsistent statement, this document, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's two different things. These are concerning bullets. That's the only thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, are hand grenades weapons or ammunition?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can use it as ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they are grenades. Are grenades weapons, as a rule?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are defensive grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Defensive hand grenades, Mr. Fitozovic, according to your knowledge, are they weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Defensive hand grenades are ammunition, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. One moment. Mr. Fitozovic, if you're able to answer this, I would appreciate it. What is the difference between a defensive hand grenade and an offensive hand grenade? If you can help, please; if you can't, no matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Offensive hand grenades are used for attack operations, offensive operations, and defensive hand grenades are used for defence operations. But as I have already said, hand grenades can be used as ammunition. I'm quite familiar with that. It can be used as explosive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, it can be used either way. So is it true, therefore, that the grenade is the same item? If you look at it, you take the pin out, what have you, it's the same item, but it can be used to defend or to offend. But are we talking about the same item in one's hand, if it's a hand grenade? I'm uncertain. But is it the same piece of equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are talking about the same thing, same item. But this one and the same item, if you modify it, or if certain parts are missing in it, it can be used as ammunition. It can be used as a booby trap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is both the -- does both the offensive and defensive hand grenade used to kill people?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that's what it's used for, and that's why it's being made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more thing: What weapon is loaded with these grenades? Are there weapons that are used -- where these hand grenades are being used as loading material?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it can be an M-48, a Kalashnikov, or a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Franjo Piplovic from Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this gentleman's occupation? What kinds of work did he do in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he worked in Slavonski Brod, in the municipality, but I don't know what kind of a post he held there, whether he had something to do with general administrative work, defence. But I do know that he worked in the municipality in Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have information about the following: That Mr. Piplovic worked on defence matters. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you ask me about Mr. Piplovic, I said that he worked for the municipality. Whether it was administration or defence, I really can't tell you this with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name, or do you know a person with the last name Meter from Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this name is familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this gentleman personally?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this person do, Mr. Meter, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he worked in the municipality. After that he was, I think, the ambassador to Australia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Slavko Bilandzic from Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know Slavko Bilandzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Piplovic and Meter help you with arming the unit in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not help us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm the fact that on the 19th of March, 1992, you received from the HVO unit in Prud a couple of bombs, one semi-automatic rifle, and a couple of grenades?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you this with any certainty. Maybe some of my men received these items, but I am not familiar with this fact. Actually, I'm not sure. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I wonder whether you could clarify for me how a grenade can be loaded into a Kalashnikov or a semi-automatic rifle. At the moment maybe just this is my perception of weapons, but to me, a grenade is about this size and it has a pin and people throw it or they do whatever. And I just have a bit of a confusion here how a grenade, whether offensive or defensive, can be loaded into a Kalashnikov or a semi-automatic rifle. So if you could just clear that up, I would appreciate it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour. I'm not certain myself, but Mr. Fitozovic can hopefully explain this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I think you understood what the Honourable Judge was asking. So could you please explain how a hand grenade can be used as ammunition for an automatic rifle or a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will certainly explain this. In order for a defensive hand grenade to be used as ammunition, on the barrel on a semi-automatic rifle or a Kalashnikov or some other long barrel, you can put a certain object that on the back has an opening, and the size of that opening is the size of the barrel, of the end of the barrel of the weapon. And then the hand grenade is put into that object, into that mounting, and then it is -- a bullet is shot, which throws this hand grenade a certain distance, and then this hand grenade explodes. That is the simplest explanation that I can give you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just wanted to complement that, because in another case where this was being explained, it was explained that it was a hand grenade launcher. I wonder whether that's the same thing like the one you've explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could not be compared to a launcher. This was an improvised weapon, this weapon that I was talking about, a makeshift item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, while you testified here, you said that on the 10th of January, 1992, you procured a hundred kilos of explosive called Vitezit 20; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date might be wrong. Could you please check the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, okay, then. Sometime in January.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this did not happen in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when was it, then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said in mid-October. You can help me here, because in October there is a fair in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in October. What year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me the following: Where did you get this explosive from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it through private channels. That is what I said earlier. I got it privately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you when you procured this explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that Osman Mesic was with me when I received this explosive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Osman Mesic, nicknamed Semso; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that Ratif Atic was also with you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that he was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get this explosive through private channels in Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform anybody else about the procurement of this explosive? Did you say this to anybody else in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is your claim that you did not inform Mr. Sulejman Tihic about the procurement of this explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I said in the testimony earlier and during the cross-examination yesterday that I did not inform Sulejman Tihic about my activities, about what I was doing, how I was doing it, and why I was doing it. Well, he knew why I was doing it, though. But I did not tell him anything about how I was doing things and what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Fitozovic, when I ask you the question, you can just say that you did not inform him, and that is all right; that is not a problem. The last -- actually, no. I have another question here. You said in your statement that 25 kilos of explosive was found in your apartment, in the bed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is in my 1995 statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 13th, 14th, 15th of February?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not see this statement of mine until I arrived here in The Hague. When I arrived, I called up Sarajevo. I called my wife and asked her if the explosive was there. True, the explosive used to be in my house, but at that time it was not there. When I say "at that time," I meanwhile my apartment was looted. It was not in my bedroom at that time, because it was moved the same moment when, in the close proximity of my bedroom, Grga Zubak's house was blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place this explosive in the emptied and dried septic tank of Tihic Pasaga from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic. The 20 kilos I gave to Odzak, and I put 80 kilos into the emptied-out and dried septic tank that belonged to another man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question that has to do with the weapons: On the 14th [As interpreted] of April, 1992, weapons also arrived into the TO staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were 50 Kalashnikovs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Pisarevic said 15th of April, and here it says "14th of April." So just to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, the question -- the date was 15th April, not 14th April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's consistent, Your Honour, with the testimony that came out yesterday, the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 15th of April. That's the correct date. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that Sabanovic Fadil participated in the bringing of these weapons, together with Salkic Ibrahim, called Ibela; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have information that along with Salkic Ibrahim, also Jasenica Fuad participated in the bringing of these weapons.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Tihic issued a receipt of SDA to Mr. Salkic Ibrahim and Jasenica Fuad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If I recall Mr. Tihic's testimony, I believe he claimed that was a forged document, number one; and number two, what he is trying to do is somehow impeach this witness through a prior statement of Mr. Tihic. And number one, a statement that Tihic -- a document that Tihic claims is a forgery. If that's -- there was the Bicic document that Tihic claimed was a forgery, but Tihic claimed this didn't happen, if I'm -- maybe I'm wrong, but I think he's trying to question this document -- question this witness about a statement that Tihic made, he can't do it in this manner. Basically he's trying to have two witnesses discuss --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is slightly different, Mr. Weiner, because the way the question has been framed is: "Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Tihic..." It's being put to him as a fact by the Defence, so it's slightly different. The way it's phrased is all right. The witness should be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you can repeat your question. Then the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, are you familiar with the fact that Mr. Tihic issued a receipt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's different. Don't put in the word "familiar." Just ask him the way you did: Are you aware. Because that's how your question came out. Your question was: "Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Tihic issued a receipt of SDA to Mr. Salkic Ibrahim and Jasenica Fuad?"

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for the procurement of weapons in Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you said that you had your patrols -- did your patrols receive any remuneration for their work?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They began receiving remuneration in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Fitozovic, receive any remuneration for your work?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, on the 25th of December, 1991, I lost my job. So in 1992, on two or three occasions, I received payments, salary, from the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain to me this salary? Who determined your salary, the amount that you would receive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amount of my salary was dictated by the amount that was available to be dispensed at that time. It was not a significant amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the funds were paid to you from the account and from the funds of the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was paid at the cash desk of the SDA. So it was paid from the petty cash, by the cashier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the name of the cashier Hata Barjaktarevic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She was the secretary and the treasurer who was employed full time as a professional in the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to correct you. She was a technical secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. My mistake. She was a technical secretary. Do you know whether anybody else from the members of the SDA, apart from the patrol members and yourself, received any remuneration for their work?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I would really like to answer your question. So I received the salary in March; the patrols received some certain amounts. I don't know if you are leading to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not. So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we will go on to an event that happened in December 1991, in Mitra Trifunovic Uco memorial home. It is the meeting of the reserve officers. You remember that you talked about it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were two meetings. We talked about one meeting and we didn't discuss the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly, Mr. Fitozovic. We will get to that other one too.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With all the other reserve officers, you duly received the invitation to attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The meeting was convened and organised by the secretariat for the National Defence and the command, or rather, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but probably they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the reserve officers in fact include both non-commissioned and commissioned officers and those with the ranks of high officers, senior officers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the term "reserve military officer" includes non-commissioned officers, officers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Now I understand. You are correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you talked about the participation of members of various ethnic groups among the attendees of the reserve officers' school, I will ask you if you're familiar with the fact that between 1980 and 1990, that 33 Croats, 7 Muslims, and 27 Serbs graduated from the reserve officers' school.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this fact, but I do know that in the engineer section of the reserve officers' school, that Suljo Zurapovic graduated from the school in 1955 and that I was the first person from Bosanski Samac to graduate from that school in 1979. So almost 24 years passed, if my calculation is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that, but Suljo Zurapovic is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So it took 25 years between the two persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I did not ask you about the sections for each arm of the armed service. I asked you for the whole school.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same thing went for all the other arms of the armed service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would this ratio correspond to the ethnic composition of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this ratio does not correspond to the ethnic composition in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I read this information correctly, the largest number --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry. You see this information? I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I'm just wondering: These statistics of graduation from the officers' -- the reserve officers' school, I think the witness has just correctly said you have the figures, he doesn't. Are you asking him to speculate? I'm not sort of entirely happy with the figures, because how does he know how many people graduated in any given year unless somehow he's privy to that information? So maybe you can explain. Maybe I'm missing something. But maybe you can explain why this line of questioning is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour. I asked the witness whether he is aware of the fact --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are not aware of the fact, please say so. You said that in the former Yugoslavia there was some kind of discrimination based on the ethnicity when it came to sending people to attend the reserve officer's school, and that's why I asked you if you are aware of the fact. And if I'm not mistaken, you graduated from the reserve officers' school in that period. You were active in the association of reserve officers, you were a member of that association. But just say. If you don't know, say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, my suggestion is that you leave this topic aside, because I graduated from the reserve officers' school in 1979, and I told you that before that time, no Muslim had graduated from that school. The last Muslim to graduate was in 1955. So what was the structure like, the ethnic structure, in the period between 1980 and 1990, I don't know, and I cannot trust this information that you provided to me. Because I also have access to some databases, and perhaps then we can compare our data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you don't know, and the moment you say you don't know, we'll leave the topic aside.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but now you're quoting data that nobody apart from you knows. 33 per cent, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You perhaps didn't understand me correctly. I said that 33 Croats, 7 Muslims, 27 Serbs, graduated from the reserve officer's school?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're on page 21 at page 19, line 11. The witness indicated he didn't know and we're still going back and forth into now just an argument over whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel, can we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have moved on. I will no longer discuss this topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that when people were summoned to attend this meeting in October - I'm sorry - in December, no discrimination was made on the basis of ethnic background when it came to summoning reserve officers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them were summoned, and I know the reason why everybody was summoned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the officers and non-commissioned officers who were present there, were they invited to join the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it said at the meeting that military officers were needed because a detachment of the JNA would be established for Bosanski Samac? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already established, and it was an attempt to legalise it at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain that term, to "legalise"? What is illegal and what is illegal here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, until that time the 4th Detachment already existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say that. I simply asked you whether it was said at that meeting such-and-such a thing was said. If you remember, say "yes"; if you don't remember, say "I don't remember" or say you don't know. Whether it was said that military officers would be needed because a detachment of the JNA would be established for the town of Bosanski Samac, which would be part of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To continue with my answer, that there were enough people, there were enough weapons, and that if this thing doesn't go that way, then there would be blood up to our knees. That's what Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic said at that time. He said we would be in blood up to our knees, and he used the Ekavian dialect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say at that time, when he invited you to join the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that those who refused to accept the invitation, he saw what was going on. He said there would be blood up to your knees here. I know who ended up in blood and who didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the commander, Lieutenant Nikolic, say that? In fact, when he said that, he said that in order to have you, the reserve officers, join the JNA and to avoid having blood up to your knees.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that in order to intimidate us, to frighten us with a show force, but he failed to intimidate me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't think this witness can really answer what the intentions were of Colonel Nikolic. I think if Defence wants to call him as a witness and have him explain what he meant when he warned these people that there would be blood up to their knees, that's their option, but it's not a valid question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, are you aware of the fact that the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army, belonging to the 17th Tactical Group, was established pursuant to an order of the 17th Tactical Group dated 5th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the municipality of Bosanski Samac, in 1991 and 1992, was in the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army? Do you know or is it that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, because I wasn't concentrating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll take it slowly. Are you aware of the fact that the municipality or the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac was in the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you aware of the fact that the order issued by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA about the formation of the 4th Detachment was publicly broadcast in the media?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that the secretariat of the National Defence ordered a mobilisation of all the conscripts and carried out the mobilisation of all the conscripts from the municipality or from the town of Bosanski Samac to fill in the ranks of the 4th Detachment of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On what date was it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, after it was established. That would be in the period in January 1992.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment existed from 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was whether you are aware of the fact that in January 1992, mobilisation was carried out, where conscripts were mobilised into the 4th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA. Are you aware of the fact or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment of the 17th TG, Tactical Group, was the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're also probably aware of the fact that the secretary of the secretariat of the municipal for National Defence, in 1991 and 1992, was Mr. Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. I wonder whether you could clarify with the witness his answer, page 24, line 22. His answer is: "Probably, yes." "Probably" raises an element of doubt. Is it, to use your phrase, "yes," "no," or "I don't know." "Probably, yes" is a little bit vague, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to clarify this matter immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, did the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA include the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have access to the document of the 17th Tactical Group, so I do not know whether Bosanski Samac was part of the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group. But let me explain something else. I'm not clear about this question that you asked me about the mobilisation that was done by the secretariat for National Defence. Who received the draft calls as part of this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The conscripts.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother, my cousin, my closer relatives, nobody received any draft calls. Could you please tell me who from my family received these calls, who from my neighbours received them? If we're talking about mobilisation, then everybody should be mobilised and not just certain parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You asked the right question. But you are also familiar with the fact that Muslims and Croats did not respond, nor did they accept these draft calls for the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, how can they receive them when you're mentioning December of 1991, when Mr. Radovan Karadzic was there? How can they receive these calls, these draft calls?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they did not want to accept them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were you in a situation where you could hear Mr. Zaric, Mr. Simo Zaric, to hear him over the media and on public rallies explain the tasks of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had such an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amongst the members of the 4th Detachment of the JNA there were members of all ethnic groups: Serbs, Muslims, Croats, and others. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that list with me, and I cannot answer this question. So my answer would be no, because I don't know the percentages. I agreed with you yesterday when you mentioned the 98 percentage point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not interested in the percentages.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you're the one that insisted on the percentages. You mentioned the 98 per cent, and I checked that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, don't argue with the witness. If he gives you an answer you don't like, you don't argue with him. And please, do remember to pause, otherwise the record won't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your admonition, Your Honour. I will try to do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the fact that members of all ethnic groups were part of the 4th Detachment: Serbs, Muslims, and Croats alike?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fitozovic, you have never seen a list of members of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in any official way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you also did not see a line-up of the entire 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I did not see the entire 4th Detachment lined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Pisarevic, I wonder whether you could ask the witness to elaborate on his answer to your question. Page 27, line 7, in response to you asking him whether he had seen lists of members of the 4th Detachment, he said: "Not in an official way." Could we have a little bit of elaboration on that point, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, did you see a list of the members of the 4th Detachment through some kind of an unofficial channel?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it through an unofficial channel, but not the full list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not see the whole list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: A supplementary question: Mr. Fitozovic, how did you know that you were not seeing the whole list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew it because of the number of the people that were on that list, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this list that you saw, how many people were on it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 350.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree, then, that the 4th Detachment had more than 350 members?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that members of the 4th Detachment of the JNA wore JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of the fact that they wore camouflage uniforms of the JNA, and members of other detachments of the JNA wore grey/green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is your claim, if I understood you correctly, that the members of the 4th Detachment did not wear uniforms of the JNA that are called SMB, or olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I saw them, they did not wear the SMB uniforms; they wore camouflage uniforms, Mr. Pisarevic. I hope this is going to make it easier for you to understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you see them, this was after the 17th, is that correct, the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th of April and later. I saw it on Cviko Tesic, Fadil Topcagic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw only a few members of the 4th Detachment, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "a few"? How many?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just the people that you listed.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't list all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many did you see?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those eight days I saw about 220 maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is your claim that you saw all of them, all the 220 members, wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, Murata Focakovic and Fadil Topcagic I saw on the 18th of April. They were mobilising Muharem, nicknamed Sovura. I can't remember his last name. The man came out in a camouflage uniform and they put a white armband on him. Murata and Fadil did that on the 18th of April, and they came in a yellow Mercedes. The same day, in the afternoon, on the other side of the yard, Cviko Tesic, again wearing a camouflage uniform and a red beret, with members of Arkan's units, or Grey Wolves, that had camouflage marks on their faces, came from the courtyard of Vlado Vrdoljak, and they were mobilising some people there. And at the same time, he said to Vlado, "Please get that pistol." I saw this with my very own eyes, and there are notes from the attic that I made. I am very sorry about this. I don't have them here. But I wrote down every day what I saw and who I saw, and I have these notes here [as interpreted], and you can -- but that doesn't matter right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Trial Chamber to notify in the record that he showed that he saw Muharem Kapetanovic, while he was being mobilised, in a uniform that was a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I saying this correctly? And that a white armband was being put on his left arm, above the elbow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I say this right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correction. Muharem Sovura received a rifle, and he had the armband, but he did not wear a camouflage uniform. I apologise to the Chamber. But that happened just in one day, in one hour, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Chamber that it be reflected that he pointed at the left arm, above the elbow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For the white armband?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this uniform and this cap that Cviko Tesic was wearing, who is from Bosanski Samac, this is not a uniform of the regular JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of the regular, but of the elite troops of the JNA. Not of the regular troops of the JNA but of the elite troops of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your opinion, Cviko Tesic belonged to this elite unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that he belonged to an elite unit. The 4th Detachment. I would not consider it an elite unit. But he wore an elite unit uniform, a uniform of an elite unit of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could these uniforms be obtained somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be obtained in the warehouses of the JNA. You could also get it in the 4th Detachment and in other detachments. It could also be bought from Arkan's and Seselj's members, because everybody wanted to be trendy; at least, they wanted their uniforms to be trendy in such a small town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I only asked you about the regular troops, the regular JNA. Did the other militaries in the former Yugoslavia have such colourful uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're going to talk about some events in Samac in 1991 and 1992. You said that there had been some sabotages in various buildings, both state-owned and private, in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your patrols were in the town 24 hours, 24/7, both day and night, and at night the number of the patrols was increased; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The number of the patrols increased just before the aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your patrols cooperate with the police, with the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not any particular cooperation. It wasn't any official kind of cooperation. Only if a person that was in the patrol and the reserve officer knew each other, then they would sort of cooperate. That was the only way there was any cooperation. But there was no official cooperation that you could see in any kind of paperwork or documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your patrols didn't submit any kind of reports to the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these patrols report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction. The witness said "to me."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these patrols were under your control?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were under my control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that we again need a clarification. What I heard as the answer of the witness on the question: "Did these patrols report to anybody?" He said: "To me." That's what I heard. And here it says: "No."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters put in a correction that the witness said: "To me." So the correct answer is on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether the police in Bosanski Samac detected any perpetrator of any order of the sabotage acts that were committed in the municipality of Bosanski Samac and in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that in 1991 and 1992, Mr. Miko Dragicevic was the police chief and he was followed by Mr. Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mention 1991 and 1992. Mr. Dragan Lukac --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's not important how many days. The important thing is that he was.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the period of four or five days, in April. It is important, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Dragan Lukac was the chief of the secret service [As interpreted] in the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Lukac and Mr. Niko Dragicevic, the police chief, were ethnic Croats?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is suggested here that there is a mistake in interpretation. I didn't say "secret service," but criminal investigation section?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which line?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies from the interpreters. We didn't hear the counsel because he was speaking quite fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Page 33, line 6. Here it said "secret service," and actually the correct translation would be "criminal investigations." That's what Mr. Pisarevic asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So it should be -- yes. Maybe if the question is asked -- let me see. Okay. The witness answered, because he understood the language, like for us who understood the interpretation. All right. It's been corrected. So it's the criminal investigations instead of the secret service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in 1992, police officers, both in the regular police and in the reserve police, were mostly Muslims and Croats? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were also ethnic Serbs. But after the visit of Radovan Karadzic to the memorial home, they separated, and they established a separate Serb reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you want to say that from that moment on, the police in Samac was composed mostly of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we will be discussing an event that took place on the 22nd of March. It is an event involving roadblocks. We can agree that the roadblocks were manned by members of your unit, members of the SDA party, and some members of the reserve police of the Samac police station, all of them ethnic Muslims.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the roadblocks set up at the entrances to the Bosanski Samac town, erected between the 21st and the 22nd of March, 1992, were manned by members of your unit, some SDA party members, members of the reserve police from the Bosanski Samac police station, and that all of them were ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's asking several questions, number one; number two, he's saying members of the SDA. Does he mean people who were there as individuals or is he saying people who were there sent by the SDA? That can have many different inferences based on a response to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel. I think it's better to split up your questions so that the questions are clear as to what you are discussing with the witness before he can answer. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Since it's time for the break anyways, I was just going to -- excuse me. I figured since it was time for the break, I've gone over every document supplied to me yesterday by Mr. Pantelic. I have one more Pantelic document. I have two documents from Mr. Lukic, and then he just gave another one today, so I would need ten minutes to talk to the witness and show him the him the new document that was supplied today to the Prosecution as well as the three other documents, authorisation to meet with the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead and discuss those with the witness. We shall have our break and continue the proceedings at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, we started discussing the roadblocks. My next question pertaining to this issue: Is it correct that the persons manning the roadblocks were under the influence of alcoholic beverages?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at that time, Mr. Osman Mesic fired shots from a Kalashnikov near the Muslim cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Izet Izetbegovic, the vice-president of the SDA party, went to the garrison in Brcko that morning to seek -- to request that the army do not intervene to remove the roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are not aware of the fact that Mr. Sulejman Tihic, the president of the Samac SDA, sent Mr. Izetbegovic, the vice-president of the Samac SDA, to the garrison of the SDA in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as we know, the roadblocks were removed on the orders of Mr. Sulejman Tihic, the president of the SDA. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not removed on the orders of Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me: Who ordered that the roadblocks be removed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I ordered that the roadblocks be removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sulejman Tihic appear at the roadblocks at any time during that day?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was -- as far as I know, he was in Pelagicevo with Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know that on that day, the 22nd of March, Sulejman Tihic was at the roadblocks in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the paramilitary units that existed in the Croat villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac were mobilised to provide support to your operation involving the setting up of the roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you did not set up the roadblocks at the entrance of Bosanski Samac from the direction of the village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you erected the roadblocks only on the access routes or entrances to the town from which Serbs can enter into the town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We set up the roadblocks at the entrances to the town, where Croats, mostly Croats, and Serbs entered the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not allow Serbs to enter the town at the roadblocks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not allow anyone to enter the town, with the exception of one case, when Mr. Marko Bozanovic was allowed to enter the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Marko Bozanovic is a Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was later to become the commander of the Territorial Defence staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any organ of the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac discuss or assess the effects achieved by the setting up of the roadblocks at the entrances to the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I did not attend those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Fitozovic, make any kind of analysis of these events?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did make an analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will move on to another topic, and that is the cooperation between the SDA and the HDZ. Are you aware of the fact that there were frequent meetings held at the highest level between the representatives of the Croatian Democratic Union and the Party of Democratic Action in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such meetings, one or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, Mr. Tihic, and Mr. Izetbegovic were in most cases members of the negotiating team on the part of the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, then: Who was in the delegation that took part in the negotiations that took place at the meetings held with the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it because you were the commander of the armed unit and the chairman of the safety and security commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Tihic was in charge of the political aspect of the work of the SDA and I took care of other business unrelated to the SDA, Mr. Tihic went to the political negotiations and talks. On one or two occasions I was there together with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were meetings where political issues were discussed. But Mr. Fitozovic, which topics were discussed at those other meetings and in other contacts that you had?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation, the security situation in the municipality, was discussed. That's what was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a meeting held on the 19th of March, 1992, in the Croatian village of Prud, with the leadership of the municipal board of the HDZ, where you were the first to arrive, and the vice-president of the SDA, Mr. Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that in the course of that meeting, Mr. Sulejman Tihic joined you, the president of the town board of the Bosanski Samac SDA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Mr. Tihic did join us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on behalf of the HDZ of the municipality of Samac, there were Mr. Panic [phoen], the president of the municipal board of the HDZ --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the name, the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mato Nujic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the first name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Filip Evic, the president of the municipal board of the HDZ for the Bosanski Samac municipality. Was Mr. Evic there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mato Madjarevic there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I thought that you would ask the question in full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mato Nujic, was he there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavko Matic, was he there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Grga Zubak?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Grga Zubak was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Vinko Dragicevic, the police chief in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I would really like to answer your question. I would like to be able to tell you that I remember, but I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay. Was Marko Bozanovic there at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Kobas Ivo there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He in particular was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Miso Mijic, from Grebnice, there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, it's really difficult for me to answer such questions. It took place a long time ago. If you ask me whether a meeting was held in Prud, I said yes. If you mention a few names, I say yes. You can now enumerate 400 people, and perhaps I will remember two or three people. You ask me about the meeting, I say yes, it was. You ask me who came first, I say yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But do you remember whether some people from Croatia attended the meeting? And I will specify --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stjepan Blazanovic, nicknamed Braco, from Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was present. He is from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that in fact he was born in the village of Donji Hasic in Bosanski Samac and that he has a permanent residence in Slavonski Brod in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I did not check his ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a person representing the Croatian army who was addressed as Major?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the joint Crisis Staff established at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this meeting, was the commander of the paramilitary units in the Croatian villages and of your military unit, which was also a paramilitary unit, was a command established, and Bozanovic, Marko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to the characterisation of his unit as a paramilitary unit. I'm not certain what a paramilitary unit is, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It has different connotations in different places and areas. He can ask if there were -- assuming there were military units, independent military units in Croatia, he could ask about were persons representing those military units as well as someone else representing yours or someone in addition -- another representative in addition to you, of your military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We haven't heard evidence that Mr. Fitozovic did have a paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your military unit, can we call it that? Your armed unit, can we call it that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my personal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The unit that you commanded, the armed unit that was under your command.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my armed unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it agreed at that time that daily cooperation should be established between the commander of Marko Bozanovic and yourself?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't answer the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- that's what I was looking at, to see whether or not it had been answered. The question whether at that meeting was the paramilitary command units of the Croatian villages of -- and the witness says "were they established?" I think that question wasn't answered. I think if you can repeat the question, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this meeting, was it decided that Marko Bozanovic, as the commander of the Croatian armed units, and you, as the commander of your armed unit, would become one command, where Marko Bozanovic would be the commander and you would be his deputy?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic. If you let me finish, I'd like to give you -- assist you here. In this meeting, we did not discuss these issues. In the previous question you had asked the same thing, and my answer was no. Alija Fitozovic and Marko Bozanovic were not talked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
